DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Six Masks, One Empty Slot

STS-HS10-L4-10001300-HSVPA910-PZQ-GBL-01 • HS Theatre Grades 9–10 • Cultural and Historical Belief Systems in Theatre
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Every mask on that wall was built by people answering a question about what they believed. A Noh mask was carved to let a spirit speak. A Commedia mask was shaped so a whole town could recognize a character from the back row. A West African dance mask was made to carry an ancestor into a ceremony, not into a show.
If your class made a mask that told the world what your community believes, what would you carve into it?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Nadia doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Nadia is doing with evidence from the picture, and say what she is searching for.
2
What is Ravi holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Ravi is holding and explain why a theatre keeps objects like it.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing and explain how her work reaches the audience.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what place this is with at least two details, and explain what work happens here.
5
Tell me about the puzzle wall.
Look at the picture. Justify what the puzzle wall shows and explain what the class is putting together.
6
Tell me about what Sena is wearing.
Look at the picture. Justify what Sena is wearing and infer her role from what she carries.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CA Arts Standards for Theatre, Grades 9–10, Cn11.1a — Explore how cultural, global, and historical belief systems affect creative choices in a drama/theatre work. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
